Drawing on expertise across RTSL's portfolio, we bring together solutions in health system resilience and epidemic readiness, digital health and data-driven decision-making, performance measurement and improvement, and sustainable health financing. We apply these capabilities to address priority health challenges, including cardiovascular health, maternal survival and sexual and reproductive health, while strengthening health systems to deliver more equitable, effective and resilient care.  </span></p> <h3><strong><span class="EOP SCXW70040856 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}">Position Purpose</span></strong></h3> <p>The Director, Maternal & Reproductive Health will provide strategic and technical leadership for RTSL's portfolio to reduce preventable maternal deaths and improve sexual and reproductive health outcomes. The role requires deep expertise in sexual, reproductive and maternal health, strong program leadership, and the ability to translate technical evidence into practical, sustainable health system improvements.</p> <p><span data-contrast="auto"><strong>Work Location: </strong>100% Remote with travel as stated. </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto"><strong>Duration:</strong> Full-time employment for a fixed term of 24 months.</span></p> <h3><strong><span class="EOP SCXW70040856 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}">Core Duties and Responsibilities</span></strong></h3> delivery against strategic objectives.</li> <li>Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team, establishing clear responsibilities and performance expectations, overseeing staffing and talent development, addressing performance and capacity gaps, and building the capabilities needed for sustained program delivery.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Technical Leadership and Program Development</strong></h4> <ul> delivery and wider health system capabilities.</li> <li>Guide the design and implementation of country programs, identifying opportunities to strengthen government leadership, institutional approaches.</li> <li>Oversee the generation, synthesis and dissemination of evidence and practical learning to inform policy, program improvement and scale-up across countries.</li> </ul> The ability to take ownership of deliverables, manage competing priorities, and make sound engineering decisions. Clear communication and presentation skills, including the ability to explain technical work to people from different disciplines. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.<br><br>Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. </span></p></div><h2><strong>Information about the position </strong></h2> <p>As Staff / Senior Staff Security Engineer in Vinted Pay, you will be the staff-level security engineer inside our regulated payments business - and the person who makes Vinted Pay's security posture match its growth. Vinted Pay is a rare security problem in the best sense: a fintech scaling across multiple European licences at marketplace speed, where security cannot be a compliance checklist or an isolated engineering task - it has to be built into the core financial architecture. Its attack surface spans multi-region AWS infrastructure, payment pipelines and payment pages, wallets holding members' money, the cardholder and personal data behind them, and a regulatory perimeter - PCI DSS, DORA, Bank of Lithuania and FCA rules - that rises every year.</p> <p>Working at staff / senior staff level as an individual contributor embedded in the Payments Engineering leadership team, you will own the security of that whole estate. Vinted Security runs a federated model: the central team sets thresholds and provides core services (pentesting, threat intelligence, SSDLC tooling, compliance), while each business unit owns local execution. Vinted Pay already owns part of its local execution; your job is to lead and scale it - this is not a policy or audit role, it is an engineering role with a mandate: translate regulatory requirements into technical guardrails and drive practical controls alongside Vinted Pay's platform and software engineers. You will work directly with Vinted Pay's Director of Engineering and functionally with the Vinted Security senior team and your security peers in Marketplace, Vinted Go, and Platform.</p> <p>This is a build role with room to grow: you start hands-on, closing the highest-impact gaps yourself and setting direction for the security work already under way, and as the function matures you will shape and functionally lead Vinted Pay's security engineering capability.</p> <h2><strong>In this position, you’ll </strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the Vinted Pay security roadmap end to end: assess the estate, prioritise by real attack paths, and drive risks to closure - a multi-quarter roadmap that shapes how Vinted Pay defends its infrastructure and payment assets, rather than reacting to the next audit.</li> <li>Turn regulation into engineering: map PCI DSS, DORA, and Bank of Lithuania and FCA requirements into practical, automated security controls and engineering guardrails - compliance as a by-product of how Vinted Pay builds, not a parallel workstream.</li> <li>Find and close the operational blind spots: run deep technical reviews of our AWS infrastructure, payment pipelines, SIEM and logging, and vulnerability management tooling (e.g. Wiz), and fix what you find - prioritised by exposure, not by finding count.</li> <li>Own PCI DSS and data protection architecture: payment page isolation, script monitoring, data encryption, and least-privilege access across multi-region environments - and turn those controls into evidence that stands up to assessors and regulators.</li> <li>Lead cross-functional security initiatives across Payments Platform, Payments Engineering, and Group Security, and drive them to delivery - whether execution sits with partner teams or you have to write the code yourself.</li> <li>Act as the technical arm of Vinted Pay's security accountable: maintain the risk register, prepare mitigation-or-acceptance decisions against centrally set thresholds, and represent Vinted Pay in the group's security governance.</li> <li>Embed secure development into Payments engineering so security lands at design time rather than after deployment, and raise the security fluency of Vinted Pay engineers so risk-based decisions happen well without you in the room - security as a delivery enabler, not a gate.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About you </strong></h2> <ul> <li>Strong hands-on security engineering experience on a real engineering foundation - you have built or run large production systems, and you can threat-model a payment flow, find the attack path yourself, and drive or build the fix.</li> <li>Experience in regulated payments or fintech - you have worked under PCI DSS and a financial regulator (FCA, Bank of Lithuania, CSSF, or equivalent) and know how their requirements become controls engineers actually run.</li> <li>A staff- or principal-level track record - you have defined, led, and delivered major, company-wide technical initiatives, and you set security direction through software design on high-scale, distributed systems rather than from the outside.</li> <li>The range to move across the <a href="https://staffeng.com/guides/staff-archetypes/">four archetypes</a> of staff engineering - tech lead, architect, solver, right hand - picking the one the domain needs together with the Director of Engineering, not the one you prefer.</li> <li>A way of working that engineers respect: evidence over assertions, attack paths over checklists, guardrails over gates.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and translate technical risk into business consequence for senior audiences, internal and external.</li> <li>Comfortable in our stack - Ruby on Rails, Go, MySQL, Temporal, AWS, SIEM and CSPM tooling - or eager to learn it, with a real interest in security and privacy as a field and the appetite to keep growing as an engineer and leader.</li> <li>Excellent written and spoken English.</li> <li>Advantage: experience building and running systems at massive scale (2+ million requests per minute), deep knowledge of observability tooling (Kibana, Grafana, Prometheus), and a passion for introducing new practices.</li> <li>Advantage: AWS security depth (IAM, KMS, multi-account and multi-region architecture), or hands-on CSPM (e.g. Wiz) and SIEM engineering.</li> <li>Advantage: privacy engineering experience, or offensive security background or certifications (e.g. OSCP).</li> </ul> <p>If this role excites you but you don't tick every box, we'd still like to hear from you.</p> <h2><strong>Work perks  </strong></h2> <ul> <li>The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">25 working days of holiday</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Newest MacBook models</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Comprehensive Medical Insurance</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Group Life and Income Protection Insurance</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">A matched pension scheme up to a set limit</li> <li>Access to a discounted gym membership plan</li> <li>Lunch benefit per working day</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">Frequent team-building events</li> <li data-stringify-indent="0" data-stringify-border="0">A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Working at Vinted </strong></h2> <p><strong>Workation policy</strong></p> title: Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure and Efficiency
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 style="font-family: GothamBold,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif; color: #662d91;">Teamwork makes the stream work.</h2> <p> </p> <h3 style="font-family: GothamBold,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;"><strong>Roku is changing how the world watches TV</strong></h3> <p>Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.</p> <p>From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.</p> <p> </p></div><h3><strong>About the Role</strong></h3> <p>You will be a SME and technical leader in engineering Infrastructure, productivity and enterprise tooling, partnering with globally distributed Engineering, Product and Security teams and systems.</p> <p> </p> <h3><strong>What You’ll Be Doing</strong></h3> <p>Roku is seeking a world class engineer to be a true force multiplier by owning the strategy, architecture, and long-term execution of engineering infrastructure, enterprise tooling, and AI-assisted workflow automation. This architect/strategist role drives org-wide improvements in engineering productivity, delivery throughput, quality, security posture, and cost efficiency by building platforms, working practices and automation (including AI/LLM-enabled capabilities) that scale across geographies and time zones.</p> <p> </p> <p></p> <h3>How will I use AI at Roku?</h3> <p>At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact. <br>We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.</p> <p></p> <p> </p> <h3><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h3> <p><strong>AI-First Automation & Intelligent Tooling </strong></p> <ul> <li>Define and lead an <strong>AI-first automation roadmap</strong> for Engineering Infrastructure and Enterprise Tooling (e.g., reducing waste, accelerating reviews, improving incident response, increasing release confidence).</li> <li>Architect and ship <strong>AI/LLM-enabled workflow automation</strong> across the SDLC (e.g. risk assessment, automated build, test and deployment, intelligent test selection, change-impact analysis, auto-triage of build/test failures).</li> <li>Establish policies and guardrails for AI usage in internal tools: <strong>data handling, prompt/response logging, model/provider selection, evaluation, fallback behaviors, and abuse prevention</strong>.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Dev Productivity & Enterprise Tooling (Global Scale)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Set technical direction and standards for the globally used developer tools, including build systems. Source code management, branching/release strategy, and self-service support tools.</li> <li>Architect and evolve, CI/CD and build/test pipelines using <strong>Jenkins</strong>, <strong>Docker</strong>, and build systems (<strong>Bazel /BitBake/Yocto </strong> <strong>preferred</strong>) to support multi-site engineering environments.</li> <li>Own and scale test and quality workflows leveraging <strong>test management systems</strong> (e.g., <strong>TestRail</strong> or equivalent), enabling consistent traceability, reporting, and release sign-off across distributed teams.</li> <li>Drive <strong>Jira</strong> workflow design and automation (templates, guardrails, integrations) to provide consistent cross-org visibility and execution.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Workflow Automation (Cross-Functional, Cross-Geo)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and implement automation spanning <strong>Engineering, Product, Marketing, and Partners</strong> (e.g., launch readiness, certification/release checklists, partner onboarding, incident/change workflows).</li> <li>Replace manual coordination with durable automation and integrations that work reliably across regions/time zones.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Security, Cost, Performance, and Reliability (Distributed Systems)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Embed <strong>secure-by-default</strong> controls into pipelines and tooling (access control, secrets handling, audit trails, policy enforcement), including for AI-enabled systems.</li> <li>Improve build/test performance and reliability (build times, test duration, flake reduction, pipeline stability) using measurable KPIs and operational rigor.</li> <li>Drive cost efficiencies across tooling/infrastructure (compute utilization, caching strategies, license rationalization including AI/runtime costs and ROI tracking.</li> <li>This is a highly visible role and you will report directly to a Vice President of Engineering. This requires a very strong technical leader with experience in the development of consumer electronics devices. The right person for this role will have ability to collaborate well with engineering and partner teams.</li> <li>Own cross-team architectures and standards; drive adoption through influence, clear technical judgment, and sustained multi-quarter execution.</li> <li>Lead design reviews, mentor senior engineers, and unblock the hardest technical problems across distributed teams and systems.</li> <li>Provide long-term stewardship via roadmaps, operational maturity (runbooks/SLOs), and incident/postmortem practices suitable for 24/7 global operations.</li> <li>Establish yourself as the person others bring their hardest problems to</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h3><strong>We’re Excited If You Have</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s in Computer Science or Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience</li> <li>Prior experience at Staff, Principal, or Architect level</li> <li>Ownership in platform/infrastructure, developer productivity, CI/CD, build systems, or workflow automation, including work spanning globally distributed teams and systems.</li> <li>Strong, hands-on knowledge of:</li> </ul> <ul> <li> <ul> <li>Git (workflows, branching strategies, release management)</li> <li>Jenkins (CI/CD pipeline design, scaling, reliability)</li> <li>Docker containers (reproducible build/test execution)</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p>Build systems ( itBake/Yocto preferred)</p> <ul> <ul> <li>Jira (workflow design/automation, cross-team visibility)</li> <li>Test management systems (e.g., TestRail or equivalent)</li> </ul> <li>Demonstrated experience delivering automation at scale, including building platforms/components used by multiple teams.</li> <li>Strong systems thinking across security, reliability, performance, and cost tradeoffs.</li> <li>Excellent written communication (architecture docs, decision records, operating procedures).</li> <li>Experience building AI-assisted developer tooling (e.g., CI insights, test intelligence, code review automation, release risk scoring, incident copilots).</li> <li>Experience implementing evaluation/monitoring for AI systems (quality metrics, drift, offline test sets, human feedback loops).</li> <li>Extensive experience with software development on embedded Linux,  multi-process architectures and IPC mechanisms</li> <li>Experience working in large cross functional teams and ability to influence teams that don't report to you</li> <li>Ability to see the big picture while focused on short-term objectives and deliverables</li> <li>Ability to multi-task and drive parallel projects and distributed teams with tight deadlines</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h6>#LI-NM1</h6><div class="content-conclusion"><h3><strong><span style="font-family: GothamBold, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;">What's Roku's approach to hybrid Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.</p> <p> </p> <h3 style="font-family: GothamBold,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;"><strong>What are some of the benefits?</strong></h3> <p>Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. title: AI Research Engineer, Pre-Training
description:
<p>Hudson River Trading (HRT) is seeking an AI Research Engineer (<strong>Pre-training</strong>) to join the HAIL team. HAIL (HRT AI Labs) is the team at HRT responsible for developing and maintaining our most powerful models, which are used by our trading teams to drive a significant fraction of our trading. We are building and deploying "foundation models for markets", that ingest and train on vast amounts of market and “alternative” data (such as language) to make predictions about future market state.</p> <p>As a <strong>pre-training</strong> research engineer on HAIL, you will have a general mandate to improve all aspects of large-scale model training, including but not limited to kernel development, training data loading, parallelism, networking, and fault-tolerance. You will work closely with our researchers to co-design and improve our models, and shape the research agenda.</p> <p>We have multiple large, modern, and rapidly growing GPU clusters, and we maintain a very high GPU-to-researcher ratio. We are simultaneously pursuing multiple strategies and developing many model types with different purposes, and we are strongly incentivized to squeeze as much as we can out of our systems. Your work will be directly, clearly, and highly impactful on the business, and it will be challenging: this is a field with no easy or obvious solutions.</p> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong engineering skills, especially any of: CUDA/Triton/Pallas/CuTe DSL kernel development, lower-level PyTorch/JAX/XLA development, CUDA Graphs, FPGA/ASIC experience</li> <li>Must have two or more years work experience building deep learning systems, for any domain: robotics, biology, chemistry, physics, audio, video, recommendations, etc.</li> <li>Experience translating methods between areas of application is highly valued</li> <li>LLM experience is valuable, but not necessary</li> <li>Finance experience is not required</li> </ul> <p>The estimated base salary range for this position is 250,000 to 300,000 USD per year (or local equivalent). title: Senior Product Manager
description: About Motorway Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding. This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better. About the role We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Motorway's Product & Engineering team. Motorway is a UK online car-selling platform connecting private sellers with ~7,500 verified dealers through online auctions. You will own a problem area end to end, in either the seller or the dealer side of the marketplace, and be accountable for the outcomes you deliver. Building is cheaper than it has ever been. The hard part now is choosing the right thing to build. We want PMs with exceptional product sense who find the problems worth solving, back that judgement with evidence, and use the latest technology to solve them in ways that weren't possible a year ago. What you will do Find the problems that matter Identify the highest-impact problem areas by combining quantitative analysis with qualitative research, and explain clearly why they matter more than the alternatives See through the hundreds of good ideas to the few that will move the business and create real value for sellers and dealers Own outcome-based goals and metrics, not feature lists Build with AI, in your work and in our product Use AI to make yourself and your team faster: automate routine PM tasks, analyse data and research quickly, and prototype or vibe code solutions to get customer feedback in days, not weeks Ask how each product could be built differently given what AI makes possible, and bring those ideas to your squad Make your team 2x more effective, not 2x busier Deliver with rigour Lead a cross-functional squad of engineers, designers and data specialists from discovery through launch and measurement Run experiments that produce learning even when they fail, and act on what you learn Make clear trade-offs between customer needs, technical constraints and business priorities Bring people with you Communicate the what, the why and the how clearly, through crisp, data-led documents and conversations Work with the people closest to you (engineering, design, data) and with execs and other business units such as Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Marketing Influence without authority and build alignment on difficult decisions Requirements Proven experience as a product manager, with a track record of shipping products that moved meaningful business metrics, not just delivering features Strong product sense. You can show how you found and prioritised the right problem, and what you chose not to do Comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative evidence: you run user research and also query data, design experiments and interpret results yourself Data-oriented. You use data to understand problems, set goals and measure impact, and can debate approaches with data scientists and analysts AI-forward. You use AI tools regularly in your own work and have hands-on experience prototyping or building with them. You have a point of view on where AI helps and where it doesn't A clear, confident communicator who can work with engineers and analysts day to day and with senior leaders across the business Ability to move between detail and strategy without losing coherence Self-starter with strong ownership, a curious mindset, and the ability to build domain knowledge quickly Experience in marketplaces, consumer products or B2B platforms is helpful but not essential You're excited about changing how people buy and sell cars Benefits We offer a fantastic range of benefits to help you thrive: Hybrid work schedule with 2 days per week in our Central London office, with regular social events, office drinks and free snacks to keep you going Great work-life balance Stock options so you can share in Motorway's growth and future success Pension scheme to plan for your future with our provider NEST Strong commitment to your personal development including budget for books, courses, conferences, etc Opt-in comprehensive health insurance through BUPA including dental care and fitness discounts Cycle to work scheme, save big ££ on a new bike and accessories One paid volunteering day a year for you to use as you wish Generous parental benefits including 6 months full paid maternity leave, 4 weeks paternity leave and workplace nursery scheme... and much more! description: Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
description: Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing. Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products. We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing. Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn. The role Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced. The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do. This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is. How we work We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out. You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production. What you'll work on first In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you: Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews. Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on. Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. description: Job Title: Regional Sales Director, Private Sector (Financial Services), NEMEA Location: London, United Kingdom The Chainalysis Private Sector team helps financial services organizations understand blockchain activity, manage financial crime risk, and adopt digital assets with confidence. Across NEMEA, we work with banks, fintechs, payments businesses, and digital asset companies to address compliance, fraud, and investigation needs. Our sales team partners with specialists across the business to connect customer priorities with the right blockchain intelligence solutions. As Regional Sales Director, you lead and develop the Private Sector Financial Services sales team across NEMEA from London. You own the regional sales strategy and revenue performance, combining disciplined execution with hands-on support for complex enterprise deals. You build senior customer relationships and help the team translate financial crime challenges and digital asset opportunities into clear business value. You create an accountable, collaborative environment where sales executives develop their skills and consistently deliver results. In this role, you'll: Lead, coach, and develop a team of sales executives to meet and exceed individual and regional revenue targets. Define and execute the NEMEA financial services sales strategy, prioritizing markets, customer segments, and accounts based on opportunity and customer needs. Own regional bookings and annual recurring revenue targets, balancing new customer acquisition with expansion across existing accounts. Build qualified pipeline through account planning, targeted prospecting, and coordinated engagement with Marketing, Sales Development, and partners. Guide complex enterprise sales cycles from discovery through negotiation and close, engaging compliance, fraud, risk, investigations, technology, procurement, and executive stakeholders. Build relationships with senior financial services decision-makers and help customers connect blockchain intelligence to their business objectives. Maintain accurate forecasts and Salesforce records, using pipeline reviews and sales activity data to identify risks and coach the team. Partner with Solutions Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and other specialists to develop customer solutions, support adoption, and identify expansion opportunities. Stay current on digital asset adoption, financial crime trends, and relevant UK and European regulatory developments to inform account strategies and customer conversations. Recruit and onboard sales executives, establish clear expectations, and build a collaborative team culture across the region. We're looking for candidates who have: 7+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS sales experience, including at least 3 years leading and developing quota-carrying sales teams. A record of meeting or exceeding multimillion annual recurring revenue targets in complex, consultative sales environments. Experience selling technology or data solutions to financial services organizations, including banks, fintechs, or payments businesses. Experience engaging compliance, financial crime, fraud, risk, or investigations teams and translating their needs into a business case. Experience leading sales across multiple markets, with an understanding of the UK and broader NEMEA financial services landscape. Demonstrated ability to coach sales executives, recruit talent, and manage performance against clear goals. Strong executive communication and negotiation skills, with experience managing complex procurement processes and multiple decision-makers. Proficiency in Salesforce and sales analytics, with a disciplined approach to pipeline management, forecasting, and account planning. Nice to have experience: Experience selling blockchain intelligence, financial crime analytics, fraud prevention, or RegTech solutions. Knowledge of digital assets, stablecoins, and blockchain use cases in banking and payments. Familiarity with UK digital asset regulation, EU MiCA requirements, AML/KYC obligations, and FATF guidance. An established network of financial services relationships across EMEA, additional regional language skills, or experience developing partner-led opportunities. About Chainalysis Blockchain technology is powering a growing wave of innovation. Businesses and governments around the world are using blockchains to make banking more efficient, connect with their customers, and investigate criminal cases. As adoption of blockchain technology grows, more and more organizations seek access to all this ecosystem has to offer. That’s where Chainalysis comes in. We provide complete knowledge of what’s happening on blockchains through our data, services, and solutions. With Chainalysis, organizations can navigate blockchains safely and with confidence. You belong here. At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. title: AI Engineer
description: <h2>Opportunity</h2> <p>Brunswick is on an exciting journey to harness the power of artificial intelligence and data science to enhance the way we work and the advice we provide to clients. As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we are looking for an AI Engineer to join our growing team.</p> <p>In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining AI-powered applications that deliver real value across the business. Working closely with our existing AI team, you will help build innovative solutions using modern AI technologies, with a particular focus on large language models (LLMs).</p> <p>This is an excellent opportunity for someone with hands-on experience developing and deploying AI applications who enjoys solving complex problems, working with a high degree of autonomy, and turning emerging technologies into practical, high-quality products.</p> <p>You will thrive in this role if you are curious, creative, and passionate about applying AI to solve real-world business challenges. You take pride in writing robust, maintainable code and enjoy collaborating with colleagues to continuously improve and expand our AI capabilities.</p> <h2>About the Role</h2> <p>Your main responsibilities will include:</p> <ul> <li>Support, run, and iterate existing AI applications.</li> <li>Design, develop, deploy, and maintain new AI applications which can be scaled across multiple business use cases, driving operational and commercial outcomes.</li> <li>Trial and test solutions with end users to iterate and optimise them.</li> <li>Research and analyse data sets using a variety of statistical and machine learning techniques.</li> <li>Track and understand the evolving AI landscape.</li> </ul> <h2>What We’re Looking For</h2> <p>The successful candidate will be a highly professional, well-rounded individual with strong problem-solving skills, engineering expertise, strategic thinking, and excellent interpersonal skills. They will have a strong academic background complemented by an outstanding career to date. Standout candidates will demonstrate:</p> <ul> <li>Experience building solutions with large language models (LLMs) and a deep understanding of the broader generative AI landscape.</li> <li>Experience designing datasets, conducting model evaluations, and fine-tuning foundation models to improve task-specific performance.</li> <li>Strong Python development skills, including experience writing production-quality code.</li> <li>Experience with front-end technologies such as JavaScript, React, HTML, and CSS.</li> <li>A solid understanding of statistics and machine learning fundamentals.</li> <li>An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline, such as Mathematics or Computer Science, or equivalent relevant industry experience.</li> <li>Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.</li> <li>The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with changing priorities and an iterative, user-focused approach to development.</li> <li>Curiosity, a strong sense of ownership, and the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.</li> <li>Previous experience in professional services would be advantageous.</li> <li>Experience developing cloud applications on Microsoft Azure would be advantageous.</li> <li>Experience with DevOps practices and tools (e.g. CI/CD, Git) would be desirable.</li> <li>Knowledge of, or experience with, secure software development practices would be advantageous.</li> </ul> <h2>Why Join Us</h2> <p>Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h1>About Brunswick</h1> <p>Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. </p> <p>Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.</p> <p>Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. </p> <p> </p> <p><em>Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our <a href="https://www.brunswickgroup.com/app/uploads/Group-Privacy-Notice-for-Employees_April-2026.pdf" target="_blank">Global Privacy Notice</a> to understand how your data is managed.</em></p> <p> </p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer - Pricing
description: 📈 Who We Are: We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. We're rebuilding how energy is bought and sold. That means cutting out middlemen, connecting businesses directly with renewable generators, and ensuring every transaction is traceable and transparent . We're a 160+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites , with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far. We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy. The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards , came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 . Learn more about us on our website . 🏅 The Role: We're hiring a Staff Machine Learning Engineer (L4) for Pricing in Rosso. Rosso is tem's core IP. It forecasts prices and volumes, holds a live view of our portfolio, and sets the fees on every quote. You'll join the pricing ML team and own key components of our dynamic pricing system. The direction is set. Within your components, choosing the bets and proving whether they worked is yours. This is a hands-on role. Most of your week will be writing and shipping production code, and you'll stay accountable for what that code does once it's live. You will: Own key components of our dynamic pricing system end to end, from design through to running them in production. Choose the bets within those components most likely to reduce sales adjustment, and show whether they worked. Make your components observable, guarded and replayable, so a wrong price is caught before a customer sees it. Unblock your own delivery across engineering, platform and commercial teams. You will report into the ML Leader for Rosso. 🚀 Responsibilities: Own key components of dynamic pricing Take ownership of one or more core components, such as the models that learn from won and lost deals, the experimentation and measurement layer, or the live guardrails that keep price changes safe. Within your components, choose between competing bets based on which is most likely to move the metric, and stop the ones that don't. Design experiments and holdouts that work with low-volume, high-value deals, where a textbook A/B test often isn't possible. Run it live, safely Build the monitoring, alerting, guardrails and staged release your components need. That includes detecting drift, catching runaway feedback loops and holding unexpected price moves for review. Make any pricing decision your components produce reproducible after the fact, for debugging and for regulators. Work with the Price Quoting squad and ML Platform so models are built for production from the start, not handed over at the end. Close the loop with the business Find out why sales teams adjust prices, and turn those reasons into model inputs or new bets. Explain model behaviour and trade-offs to engineers, product and commercial colleagues clearly enough that they can act on it. Redesign the team's recurring pricing workflows with AI built in, such as feedback triage, daily price review and experiment write-ups. Decide which steps stay human. 🎯 🎯 Requirements: Must-haves: You build. Most of your current role is writing and shipping production code, and you want to keep it that way. This is not a people leadership role or an architecture role where others implement. You have owned a live ML system that made automated decisions with money attached, for example in algorithmic trading, dynamic pricing, marketplaces, ad bidding, credit or betting. You have dealt with its failures in production, such as feedback loops, silent drift, bad outputs reaching customers and rollbacks, and changed how you build because of them. Strong probabilistic modelling and decision-making under uncertainty, such as pricing, conversion or elasticity modelling, and experimentation. You formulate the problem from first principles and pick the simplest approach that works. You've run ML as production services on modern cloud infrastructure: containerised models behind APIs, event-driven microservices, infrastructure as code and CI/CD on AWS or similar. Your model changes go through the same pipeline, tests and rollback as any other code, so shipping one on a Thursday afternoon is routine. Production-grade Python, and a habit of designing for observability, testing and replay. You work as a peer with software engineers. A track record of moving a commercial metric, working alongside product managers and commercial stakeholders to get there. You use AI tooling as a day-to-day multiplier on your own work, and you know where it fails. Energy experience is not required. We will teach you the market. What we can't teach quickly is the judgement that comes from running a live pricing or trading system. Bonus points: Experience in energy, commodities or other markets where prices, forecasts and risk interact. Contextual bandits, causal inference or Bayesian methods used in production. Stochastic optimisation or operations research. A PhD in a field such as maths, physics, computer science or operations research. ✨ Benefits & Perks: Salary: Competitive. We are looking to pay £115,000 or equivalent in local currency. Stock Options: everyone on the team has ownership in our mission. 25 days holiday + public holidays. Swap public holidays for ones that matter most to you. Plus, get an extra day off for your birthday 🎉. Remote working: we're fully remote, distributed across Europe Home working & wellbeing budgets: Up to £1,200 / €1,200 annually to upgrade your remote setup (co-working passes, equipment, etc.). Up to £150 / €150 monthly on anything that supports your wellbeing, from therapy to gym memberships to meditation apps. 🗣️ Interview Process: Our processes normally take around 2-3 weeks from first call to offer. Please let us know about any adjustments to timelines that may be required. First call with our Talent Team (30 mins). This is to understand your experience, motivations, and discuss the role in more detail. Behavioural interview with our Rosso GM, hiring manager for this role (30 mins). This is your chance to really understand the role, the expectations, and ensure alignment on ways of working. Technical interview with the Team (90 mins). You'll meet with potential peers in this session and work through a live technical exercise. Bar Raiser interview with Stakeholders (45 mins). The final session will be with two cross-functional stakeholders. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for. The Role Orbital has been scaling fast, and we’re scaling or security and compliance with it. We're hiring a senior, London-based InfoSec Lead to own our information security due diligence, compliance, and vendor risk end-to-end - bringing structure and consistency to work that's currently covered on a contractor basis. This is a full-time InfoSec role, working alongside our IT Manager. Whilst experience in IT operations or IT management is helpful, the Infosec Lead and IT Manager report independently to our Head of Operations and own separate (but naturally interconnected) remits. You’ll also work closely with Engineering, Product, Legal and our external Infosec support, to keep security and compliance embedded in how the business runs, not bolted on after the fact. What You'll Own InfoSec & Compliance Delivery You will: Own our InfoSec strategy and roadmap : set the direction for how security and compliance scale with the business, not just an executor; identify control gaps and weaknesses, prioritize remediation, and track it through to completion. Own our risk program : run risk identification, assessment and treatment, keep the risk register current. You're making the call on what's an acceptable risk. Own third party risk assurance, in both directions : run vendor security reviews for vendors we bring on (or are renewing with) and own customer & vendor due diligence (DDQs) when we’re the ones being assessed. Pull in support required from the rest of the business and jump on client calls when needed to resolve DDQs. Drive automation on the DDQ side specifically, so it doesn’t eat a disproportionate share of your time as the function matures. Own our existing and future compliance certifications: you’ll be responsible for maintaining compliance with existing standards (ISO 27001 and SOC2 Type 2) and pursuing future certifications relevant to us. Management of the compliance program will be end-to-end, and involve ISMS management reviews, quarterly access control reviews, audit evidence gathering, scheduling and remediation tracking. This also includes keeping policy & public-facing security documentation (eg. our trust centre) current - so certification is a continuously-run capability rather than a periodic scramble. Partner cross-functionally : work with Engineering, Product, and Legal to embed security and compliance requirements into how we build and sell, and stay close enough to product changes that customer-facing security information is always accurate. What We're Looking For Significant senior in-house or scale-up InfoSec leadership experience : you've owned due diligence, vendor review, and compliance work end-to-end inside a fast-moving business, not just advised from the outside. Strong understanding of cloud & cloud security, and ideally previous technical background in IT Security or SWE / DevOps. A track record of scaling due-diligence processes , not just running them manually, you know how to spot what can be templated, automated, or self-served, and you make that happen rather than just wishing for it. Comfortable being close to engineering : you don't need to write code, but you're happy sitting in technical conversations, understanding product changes, and knowing enough about IT systems to weigh in sensibly on security-sensitive changes. Pragmatic and delivery-focused : you know the difference between a genuine risk and a distraction, and you keep due diligence and audit work moving at commercial pace rather than becoming a bottleneck. AI-literacy with working familiarity with AI governance (ISO 42001, EU AI Act etc). Comfortable operating independently : this is an individual-contributor role to start, with real ownership of the roadmap rather than a narrow, audit-only remit. Working knowledge of privacy law is important (GDPR/CCPA/US state privacy laws) to partner with our legal function. Why This Might Not Be For You You want to run day-to-day IT operations or manage IT staff. That sits with our IT Manager, not this role. You prefer tasks defined and handed to you. This is a role for an independent decision maker... you're expected to identify what needs doing, set the plan, and drive it to closure yourself, not wait to be briefed. You feel more comfortable with a narrowly-defined, audit-only remit. This role sits close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, and is expected to actively reduce manual DDQ overhead over time, not just process tickets. Why Join Orbital Shape how security and compliance scale with the business... the processes and playbooks here are still being built. Genuine cross-functional influence: you'll be close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, not sitting outside them. Genuine momentum: $60m Series B, doubling headcount, expanding across two continents. Work alongside a leadership team that treats security as a business enabler, not just a risk function. 🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on. 💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. title: Senior Implementation Engineer

Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself, then choose the challenge, choose Heidi. The role The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution. You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles. Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support. You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation. Success in this role looks like: Hands-on delivery — you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done. Technical ownership — every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves. Fast unblocking — technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what. Clean boundaries — you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls. Trusted translation — customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal. This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations. What you’ll do Technical Onboarding & Account Setup Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness. Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment. Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites. Integration Delivery Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own. Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently. Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work. Product-technical Configuration Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria. Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too. Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement). Technical Escalation & Resolution During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria. Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation. Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved. Information Governance & Security Enablement Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner. Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer). Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan. Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work. title: Principal Database Engineer
description: Building the Future of Open Finance Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. The team Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform. We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work. The opportunity Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference. Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks. Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete. Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises. Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance. Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams. Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions. Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production. What you bring 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time. Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns. Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions. Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain. Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling. Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process. Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery. Nice to haves Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs. Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar). Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. title: FIX Onboarding & Client Services
description: FIX Onboarding & Client Services, EMEA Hybrid, London, UK (3+ days per week in-office) | Full-Time About Us Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers. We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems. The Role We are seeking a motivated and technically curious Onboarding and Client Services professional to join our London team. This role will focus on FIX client onboarding, integrations, and client service delivery across FX, equities and digital assets. The successful candidate will work closely with clients and internal teams to ensure seamless connectivity, smooth integration, and exceptional service throughout the client lifecycle. We're building genuinely AI-enabled tooling to support this function — so this role is less about arriving with a decade of FIX expertise already committed to memory, and much more about someone sharp, adaptable, and genuinely curious who can use that tooling to go further, faster, and think proactively about how the process itself should keep improving. What You'll Work On FIX Onboarding & Integrations: Lead and manage FIX client onboarding projects — from initial requirements gathering through certification and production go-live. Configure, test, and validate FIX sessions, including order routing, execution reporting, and market data flows. Coordinate conformance testing and certification with clients to ensure compliance with platform standards. Document onboarding procedures, client configurations, and integration best practices. Leverage internal AI and automation tools to streamline client onboarding and troubleshooting — including tooling built specifically for this function, giving you a genuine head start on deep process knowledge. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to support new FIX workflows, APIs, and client integration initiatives. Client Services: Serve as frontline technical support for clients in EMEA across FX and equities business lines. Build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring timely and transparent communication addressing their needs and queries with professionalism and efficiency. Provide ongoing technical and operational support for production trading environments. Manage client inquiries, troubleshoot workflow or configuration issues, and coordinate resolutions across internal teams. Partner with account management, sales and product teams to ensure a positive client experience and successful delivery of platform enhancements. What We Need 2-5 years of experience in a client onboarding, integration, or technical support role within financial technology, trading, or brokerage. Good working knowledge of the FIX protocol — message structures, session management, and common trading workflows. Genuine comfort troubleshooting FIX connectivity, analysing logs, and resolving integration issues, with the judgement to know when to dig deeper. Familiarity with FX and Equities trading environments, order lifecycle management, and market data connectivity — genuine interest in working across multiple asset classes rather than staying within one. A genuinely proactive, tech-first mindset — someone who treats our AI and automation tooling as a way to go further and faster, not a replacement for good judgement, and who naturally looks for ways to improve a process rather than simply following it. Excellent communication and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple onboarding/client projects in parallel. Nice-to-have: Experience with OMS/EMS platforms, liquidity aggregators, or trading system integrations. Exposure to other API protocols and architectures (REST, WebSocket) — relevant given the depth of our own API. Scripting or automation experience (e.g. Python) and familiarity with monitoring tools (Splunk, Grafana, or similar). Understanding of financial market structure and post-trade workflows. What You Get A genuinely rich API to work with — not a thin FIX wrapper bolted onto a legacy system. You'll onboard clients onto an API with real depth across order routing, execution reporting, and market data — the kind of platform where understanding the protocol properly actually matters. Breadth across FX, Equities, and digital assets — most FIX/onboarding roles sit inside a single asset class. Here you'll build knowledge across all three, at a network connecting 40+ liquidity providers — exposure that compounds faster than a single-product environment. Real ownership of the tech-to-business bridge — you're not just configuring sessions, you're the person translating FIX/API detail into client outcomes clients actually care about. That combination — technical credibility plus commercial judgement, is the actual shape of this role. A genuinely tech-first operation — we've built dedicated AI tooling for this function specifically, so your ramp-up is faster and your day-to-day is spent on the client and integration problems that need real judgement, not repetitive configuration work. A small, senior team — you'll work directly alongside Client Services, TechOps, and engineering, with real visibility into how the platform works end to end, not a large layer of process between you and the people who built it. Growth across the business — the skills this role builds (protocol depth, client-facing technical credibility, cross-asset exposure) are the same ones that open doors internally. Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites Our Hiring Process We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages. Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes S tage 2: Team Conversation with one or two members of the Client Services team Format: Video call or In-person, interactive session, ~60 minutes Stage 3: Leadership Conversation with CRO Format: Video call or In-person, ~60 minutes What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days. *Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around. How to Apply Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role. Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate. Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy . Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Sr. Compliance Consultant
description: About Us Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity. Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance. We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth. Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures. Staff TSMs take our largest, multi-site accounts and lead programs across the team.</p> <p><strong>In this role, you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the technical relationship with your customers' engineering and executive leaders, and be the person they trust to tell them what's really happening.</li> <li>Run delivery and onboarding programs end to end, from contract and site readiness to the day the customer runs production work on new capacity.</li> <li>Read each account's health every week, catch problems early, and drive cross-team issues to an owner and a resolution.</li> <li>Coordinate Fleet Operations, Capacity, data center, support and engineering teams on your customers' behalf, leading through influence.</li> <li>Carry customer needs into Product and Engineering and follow them through to a decision, then close the loop with the customer.</li> <li>Partner with account executives on one customer message, and with Specialist Field Engineers on technical depth.</li> <li>Help the team scale: improve our playbooks and tooling, interview, and mentor newer TSMs.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Who You Are</strong></h2> <ul> <li>5+ years in technical program management, technical account management, solutions architecture, customer success engineering or professional services delivery with cloud infrastructure customers.
